summary: Records IANA's allocation of a block of Diameter command codes to the Third Generation Partnership Project for its Release 5. It takes no position on how they are used, and the codes cannot be reused for later releases. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Diameter commands have numbers. This memo says a block of those numbers was set aside for one mobile phone standards group.

questions: can 3gpp release 5 diameter codes be reused
subtitle: IANA sets aside Diameter command codes 300 through 313 for 3GPP Release 5 only.

tldr.problem: The 3GPP defined Diameter applications for its IP Multimedia Subsystem in Release 5, and those applications need new Diameter command codes.
tldr.mechanism: IANA allocated Diameter command codes 300 through 313 for use in 3GPP Release 5.
tldr.outcome: The codes are for Release 5 only. The protocols were not carefully reviewed by the IETF, and later releases are expected to use standard command space with IETF documentation.

today: RFC 3589 is Informational and the metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated. The text says the codes are for Release 5 only and that later releases are expected to use other mechanisms.

sections.title: Why the Codes Were Needed
sections.content:
The Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) is defining the Internet Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) as part of its Release 5 architecture. As part of it, 3GPP defined a Diameter application that requires new Diameter command codes.

This memo does not pass judgment on how the codes are used. It records the allocation.
sections.eli5: A group building a phone network needed some new numbered buttons on a shared control panel, so it asked for a block of them.

sections.title: Command Code Allocation
sections.content:
IANA has allocated Diameter command codes 300 through 313 for use in 3GPP Release 5. These codes are intended for Release 5 only. Future 3GPP releases are expected to use alternate mechanisms, and codes for Release 6 are expected to come from the standard command space, with IETF documentation.

The RFC also warns that the protocols defined by these codes have not been carefully reviewed by the IETF community and are not considered general mechanisms appropriate for broad usage.
sections.eli5: The block of numbers is for one version only. The next version has to ask the normal way, and the numbers were not checked by everybody.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo says only that it is not known to affect the security of the Internet. It adds no mechanism of its own.
sections.eli5: Writing down who got which numbers does not open any new doors for attackers.
